newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Prods--Tight RFG supplies send Harbor up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Prods--Tight RFG supplies send Harbor up.

text.p: New York Harbor reformulated gasolines continued to skyrocket Friday, with nearby supplies commanding ever higher premiums to the NYMEX futures.
Meanwhile, U.S. Gulf and Midcontinent differentials were little changed in lackluster trading activity, market watcher said.
On the NYMEX, September gasoline futures gained 0.48 cents to settle at 66.81 cents a gallon and September heating oil futures shed 0.62 cent to finish at 55.25 cents a gallon.
NEW YORK HARBOR
Reformulated gasoline differentials extended their bullish trend, as buyers paid nearly 1.00 cent over the levels seen late Thursday, traders said.
A 125,000 barrel parceel of prompt reformulated A2 traded at 8.15 cents over the September futures early in the day, sopping up most of the available material in the region, one trader said.
A smaller parcel traded at 8.80 cents over the futures later in the day, and offers reportedly pulled back above the 9-cent level.
Prompt conventional M2 gasoline was talked between about 5.50 to 6.00 cents over the screen, according to players.

Traders continued to point to the lack of prompt barrels as the reason for surging reformulated differentials with Tosco's 110,000 barrel a day catalytic cracker down. However, that unit is scheduled to begin restarting on Saturday and may help meet some of the demand next week.
"It's really unbelieveable," one frustrated trader said. "There's no waterborne barrels available either."
U.S. GULF
Prompt regular conventional M1 gasoline differentials firmed slightly in very quiet trade late Friday amid a lack of buyers and sellers.
"There are a lot of players out of pocket," said one Gulf trader. "If someone wants to get something done he's willing to pay a little more to do it so he can start the weekend."
In late trade, M1 conventional unleaded was done at 0.40 cents under the screen, about a 0.10 cents higher than Thursday.
A 50,000-barrel parcel for the back 24th was done at 2.10 cents below the print, even with Thursday.
Traders said the market remained "sensitive" following the outage at Exxon's 110,000 barrel-per-day catalytic cracker at its Baytown, Texas refinery earlier this week.
The company reportedly purchased about one million barrels of gasoline to make up for the lost production and was not seen in the market Thursday and Friday.
However, little reaction was seen to the fire at Shell's Odessa, Texas plant, which has a capacity of about 28,000 barrels per day.

A scheduling deadline for the back 23rd heating oil did little to disturb differentials. Barrels were done at 2.60 cents under the Merc, about 0.10 cents firmer than Thursday. Barrels for delivery by Aug 21 were done at 2.50 cents under the print.
MIDCONTINENT
Midcontinent unleaded gasoline differentials were slightly weaker to steady in quiet activity, with few players in the market available due to industry outings, traders said.
Group Three unleaded was pegged a quarter cent weaker at 4.75/5.00 cents a gallon, with the any months at 2.00/2.25 cents.
Chicago material was also down at 3.25/3.50 cents, with the third cycle ranged 1.00/1.25 cents, players said.
Low sulphur diesel in Chicago continued its two-day firming trend to see deals done at even to the screen. The value is about a half cent above Thursday.
-- New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
